A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CREAM research work. The complete main texts and Appendices A–H are readable, including equations, tables and figures, and retained material can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on both FMNIST variants, CUB and CelebA, including accuracy, interventions, leakage and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on the retained datasets, including expanded baseline comparisons, computational measurements, concept-removal experiments and intervention-propagation tests.

M1.justification: v2 adds an intervention-propagation procedure: invert concept activations, recover preceding latent activations, then propagate forward to update other concepts and task predictions (Section 4.2; Appendix A.3). This substantially extends v1's CREAM interventions, which directly replace concept predictions for task inference. The underlying splitter, masked networks, joint loss and side-channel regularization remain.

E1.justification: The datasets, image populations and classification targets remain unchanged. v2 adds a limited-concept-supervision scenario on CUB by removing entire concept groups (Figure 9, left), extending incomplete-concept evaluation beyond the fixed iFMNIST setting.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates C2BM and CGM with discovered and supplied graphs on FMNIST and CelebA, and adds CBM+SC across the retained benchmarks (Table 2; Figure 6; Appendix E.2). These substantially expand the actual comparator set. Ground-truth-concept and CREAM-without-side-channel results already existed in v1's appendices. The black-box row is removed from the appendix hard-versus-soft comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix D now states that ResNet-18 uses no pretrained weights and describes CelebA training as 200 epochs rather than early stopping with a 200-epoch cap. Selected CelebA CREAM settings change from dropout 0.8 to 0.1 and total latent dimension 512 to 75. New experiments introduce controlled CPU/GPU profiling and propagation with dC=1. These are reported protocol revisions; they do not establish which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses relating CCI to intervention effectiveness, removing CUB concept groups, comparing interventions with and without side-channels, propagating indirect-concept interventions, and substituting a discovered CelebA graph (Figures 8–9; Appendices E.2, E.4 and E.6). These test substantial new questions. Existing group interventions, leakage ablations and dropout, dimensionality and depth studies are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five seeds and report means and standard deviations. v2 additionally specifies averaging computational measurements over 20 iterations after five burn-in iterations (Appendix E.1). This adds a measurement-repetition protocol, without indicating an increase in training seeds or a new general uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Many retained results change: CUB CBM task accuracy is 62.03±0.51% in v1 Table 1 and 73.76±0.32% in v2 Table 2; revised settings prevent treating this as a controlled performance gain. cFMNIST H-CREAM accuracy changes from 88.18±4.92% to 91.29±0.73% in the appendix comparison. v2 also adds comparator scores, runtime and memory results, missing-concept findings, and the finding that indirect-concept propagation yields almost no accuracy benefit.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.3 derives the conditional softmax inverse and discusses conditions for recovering exogenous activations, including dimensionality, nonzero weights and activation-range restrictions. This is a localized mathematical extension. The graph masks, training objective, leakage definition, CCI formula and CCI threshold derivation already appear in v1.

C1.justification: v2 expands the headline contribution into a modular framework accommodating prior CBM relationship structures, adds computational-efficiency claims, and emphasizes effectiveness with very limited concept supervision. Its abstract claims operation without additional computational overhead. The conclusion also qualifies leakage avoidance as occurring in specific scenarios, narrowing v1's broader leakage-free characterization.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations connecting CCI with intervenability and stronger regularization with scarce concepts. It attributes ineffective propagation to inversion problems and weak parent–child influence, recommending direct-concept interventions (Appendices A.3 and E.4). It also proposes an optimization explanation for side-channel benefits. Conversely, v1's explicit warning that misaligned expert reasoning can constrain performance is removed.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promise of code release upon acceptance with a concrete repository hyperlink. It adds exact profiling hardware, timing and memory instrumentation, execution controls, and numerical handling for inversion. Most existing implementation documentation remains; the approximate training durations and total compute estimate in v1 are removed. The linked repository's availability cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: v2 adds Parisini et al. on leakage, removes the Alvarez Melis–Jaakkola and Lakkaraju–Bastani references, and sharpens comparisons with CGM and C2BM concerning graph restrictions, computational cost and side-channel interpretability. Table 1 maps prior approaches' relationship structures into CREAM. Most cited work is retained; C2BM's publication update is not a new work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related Work moves from Section 4 to Section 2, leakage and the side-channel receive dedicated subsections, and the experimental narrative and Appendix E are reorganized. These are substantial editorial and structural changes beyond inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and typography, recolors reasoning graphs, expands and restructures tables, and adds intervention and efficiency displays. Existing CCI and dropout plots are combined with new panels, and correlation heatmaps switch from signed to absolute values with revised color scales. Several appendix results move into main-text displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by directly comparing against closely related graph-based CBMs previously only discussed, testing side-channel controls and scarce-concept settings, and documenting unsuccessful intervention propagation with explicit limitations. Computational measurements and a code-access link improve auditability. Some claims remain overstated: the abstract's no-overhead wording conflicts with Table 3's 1.82–2.46× CBM-relative GPU runtimes on FMNIST/CUB. Nevertheless, the broader comparisons and clearer empirical boundaries provide a substantial net improvement.
